Encouragement to the Faithful Remnant of Israel to Trust in God for Deliverance, Both from Their Long Babylonian Exile, and from Their Present Dispersion.</title> <div sID="gen15944" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9300"/><hi type="bold">1. me--</hi>the God of your fathers.<div eID="gen15944" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15945" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">ye ... follow after righteousness--</hi>the godly portion of the nation; <reference osisRef="Isa.51.7">Is 51:7</reference> shows this (<reference osisRef="Prov.15.9">Pr 15:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Tim.6.11">1Ti 6:11</reference>). "Ye follow righteousness," seek it therefore from Me, who "bring it near," and that a righteousness "not about to be abolished" (<reference osisRef="Isa.51.6">Is 51:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.51.7">7</reference>); look to Abraham, your father (<reference osisRef="Isa.51.2">Is 51:2</reference>), as a sample of how righteousness before Me is to be obtained; I, the same God who blessed him, will bless you at last (<reference osisRef="Isa.51.3">Is 51:3</reference>); therefore trust in Me, and fear not man's opposition (<reference osisRef="Isa.51.7">Is 51:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.8.12">8, 12</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.8.13">13</reference>). The mistake of the Jews, heretofore, has been, not in that they "followed after righteousness," but in that they followed it "by the works of the law," instead of "by faith," as Abraham did (<reference osisRef="Rom.9.31">Ro 9:31</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rom.9.32">32</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rom.10.3">10:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rom.10.4">4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rom.4.2-Rom.4.5">4:2-5</reference>).<div eID="gen15945" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15946" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">hole of ... pit--</hi>The idea is not, as it is often quoted, the inculcation of humility, by reminding men of the fallen state from which they have been taken, but that as Abraham, the quarry, as it were (compare <reference osisRef="Isa.48.1">Is 48:1</reference>), whence their nation was hewn, had been called out of a strange land to the inheritance of Canaan, and blessed by God, the same God is able to deliver and restore them also (compare <reference osisRef="Matt.3.9">Mt 3:9</reference>). <div eID="gen15946" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 51 Is 51:1-23 . Encouragement to the Faithful Remnant of Israel to Trust in God for Deliverance, Both from Their Long Babylonian Exile, and from Their Present Dispersion. 1. me-- the God of your fathers. ye ... follow after righteousness-- the godly portion of the nation; Is 51:7 shows this ( Pr 15:9 ; 1Ti 6:11 ). "Ye follow righteousness," seek it therefore from Me, who "bring it near," and that a righteousness "not about to be abolished" ( Is 51:6 , 7 ); look to Abraham, your father ( Is 51:2 ), as a sample of how righteousness before Me is to be obtained; I, the same God who blessed him, will bless you at last ( Is 51:3 ); therefore trust in Me, and fear not man's opposition ( Is 51:7 , 8, 12 , 13 ). The mistake of the Jews, heretofore, has been, not in that they "followed after righteousness," but in that they followed it "by the works of the law," instead of "by faith," as Abraham did ( Ro 9:31 , 32 ; 10:3 , 4 ; 4:2-5 ). hole of ... pit-- The idea is not, as it is often quoted, the inculcation of humility, by reminding men of the fallen state from which they have been taken, but that as Abraham, the quarry, as it were (compare Is 48:1 ), whence their nation was hewn, had been called out of a strange land to the inheritance of Canaan, and blessed by God, the same God is able to deliver and restore them also (compare Mt 3:9 ).

The sense favors Gesenius (<reference osisRef="Jer.5.22">Jr 5:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.31.35">31:35</reference>), or English Version (<reference osisRef="Isa.51.9">Is 51:9</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.51.10">10</reference>, which favors the special reference to the exodus from Egypt). <div eID="gen15986" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9316"/><div sID="gen15992" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9316"/><hi type="bold">17. Awake, awake, stand up, O Jerusalem, &c.--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Isa.52.1">Is 52:1</reference>).<div eID="gen15992" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15993" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">drunk--</hi>Jehovah's wrath is compared to an intoxicating draught because it confounds the sufferer under it, and makes him fall (<reference osisRef="Job.21.20">Job 21:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.60.3">Psa 60:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.75.8">75:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.25.15">Jr 25:15</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.25.16">16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.49.12">49:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.12.2">Zec 12:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.14.10">Re 14:10</reference>); ("poured out without mixture"; rather, "the pure wine juice mixed with intoxicating drugs").<div eID="gen15993" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15994" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">of trembling--</hi>which produced trembling or intoxication.<div eID="gen15994" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15995" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">wrung ... out--</hi>drained the last drop out; the dregs were the sediments from various substances, as honey, dates, and drugs, put into the wine to increase the strength and sweetness. <div eID="gen15995" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 17. Awake, awake, stand up, O Jerusalem, &c.-- ( Is 52:1 ). drunk-- Jehovah's wrath is compared to an intoxicating draught because it confounds the sufferer under it, and makes him fall ( Job 21:20 ; Psa 60:3 ; 75:8 ; Jr 25:15 , 16 ; 49:12 ; Zec 12:2 ; Re 14:10 ); ("poured out without mixture"; rather, "the pure wine juice mixed with intoxicating drugs"). of trembling-- which produced trembling or intoxication. wrung ... out-- drained the last drop out; the dregs were the sediments from various substances, as honey, dates, and drugs, put into the wine to increase the strength and sweetness.
entries.reader_content_plain: 17. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9317"/><div sID="gen15996" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9317"/>18. Following up the image in <reference osisRef="Isa.51.17">Is 51:17</reference>, intoxicated and confused by the cup of God's anger, she has none to guide her in her helpless state; she has not yet awakened out of the sleep caused by that draught. This cannot apply to the Babylonish captivity; for in it they had Ezekiel and Daniel, Ezra and Nehemiah, as "guides," and soon awoke out of that sleep; but it applies to the Jews now, and will be still more applicable in their coming oppression by Antichrist. <div eID="gen15996" type="x-p"/>
